questions.question: A patient with acute lymphoblastic leukemia and a central venous catheter has blood cultures growing yeast that are germ-tube negative.
questions.question_raw: A patient with ALL and a CVC. Blood cultures grow yeast that are germ tube negative.

parts.text: What two different antifungal agents could you start empirically, and give their mechanisms of action?
List two things to follow up on in addition to starting antifungals.

parts_raw.text: What 2 different antifungal agents could you start empirically (and give mechanisms of action)?
List 2 things to follow-up with in addition to starting antifungals.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) An echinocandin (e.g., caspofungin, micafungin, or anidulafungin) — inhibits beta-1,3-D-glucan synthase, blocking synthesis of an essential fungal cell-wall polymer. (2) Liposomal amphotericin B — binds ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming pores that cause leakage of cell contents and cell death. (Germ-tube negativity indicates a non-albicans species; empiric echinocandin covers likely fluconazole-resistant species such as C. krusei/C. glabrata.) b) (1) Remove the central venous catheter and repeat blood cultures every 24-48 h to document clearance. (2) Obtain a dilated ophthalmologic (fundoscopic) examination for endophthalmitis once the neutrophil count recovers, and send species identification with antifungal susceptibility testing.
questions.beyond_mandell: IDSA 2016 candidiasis guideline: echinocandin first-line for candidemia in neutropenic patients; catheter removal, follow-up cultures, and ophthalmologic exam recommended.

cohort_answer.text: Echinocandin – inhibits beta 1,3 D-glucan synthase; Amphotericin B – inhibits ergosterol synthesis which is important to maintain cell wall integrity. (C. krusei – fluconazole resistant, voriconazole/isavuconazole sensitive.) || Removal of CVC, repeat blood culture 24-48 hours after initiating antifungals; Eye exam when neutrophils recover.

questions.question: Caspofungin is an interesting antifungal drug.
questions.question_raw: Caspofungin is an interesting antifungal drug.

parts.text: What is its mechanism of action?
List 2 anatomical sites other than the central nervous system where its concentration does not reach adequate therapeutic levels.
List 3 fungi (genus) against which it is not clinically useful.

parts_raw.text: What is its mechanism of action?
List 2 anatomical sites other than the central nervous system where its concentration does not reach adequate therapeutic levels
List 3 fungus (genus) against which it is not clinically useful

questions.model_answer:
a) Non-competitive inhibition of the enzyme (1,3)-beta-D-glucan synthase, blocking synthesis of beta-1,3-D-glucan, an essential structural polymer of the fungal cell wall; glucan depletion causes osmotic instability and cell lysis (fungicidal against Candida, fungistatic against Aspergillus). Mammalian cells lack this target, accounting for low toxicity.
b) (1) Urine/urinary tract (negligible urinary concentrations). (2) Eye/vitreous.
c) (1) Cryptococcus. (2) Fusarium. (3) Mucorales/Rhizopus (zygomycetes). (Also acceptable: Trichosporon, dimorphic fungi such as Histoplasma/Blastomyces.)

cohort_answer.text: MOA: Caspofungin (echinocandins) targets fungal cell glucan synthesis by competitively inhibiting the beta-1,3-D-glucan synthase enzyme complex; beta-glucans provide structural integrity to fungal cell walls; depletion causes loss of resistance to osmotic forces and cell lysis (fungicidal). Poor penetration sites: GU system, eye. Not clinically useful against: Cryptococcus; Histoplasmosis; Blastomycosis; Sporothrix; Zygomycetes; Fusarium; Mucor. Echinocandins are primarily effective against Candida and Aspergillus, with relatively weak activity against other molds/yeasts.

questions.question: Antifungals: state the target site for posaconazole, caspofungin, terbinafine, and amphotericin B.
questions.question_raw: Q15 (2017 PM) Antifungals. Target site for: Posaconazole, Caspofungin, Terbinafine, Amphotericin

parts.text: State target site for each antifungal

parts_raw.text: State target site for each antifungal

questions.model_answer: (1) Posaconazole - lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (inhibits conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol, increasing membrane permeability). (2) Caspofungin - beta-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase (blocks cell-wall glucan synthesis, loss of osmotic integrity). (3) Terbinafine - squalene epoxidase (blocks ergosterol synthesis with toxic squalene accumulation). (4) Amphotericin B - ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane (binds ergosterol, forms pores, causing leakage of cellular contents).

cohort_answer.text: Posaconazole - lanosterol 14-alpha demethylase (inhibits conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol, increased membrane permeability, cell lysis). Caspofungin - beta-(1,3)-glucan synthase (blocks glucan cross-linking of fungal cell wall, loss of osmotic resistance, cell lysis; good vs Candida biofilms). Terbinafine - squalene epoxidase (inhibits ergosterol synthesis, causes toxic squalene accumulation). Amphotericin - ergosterol (binds ergosterol, forms pores, leakage of cellular components; lower concentrations increase K+ channel activity, higher concentrations form pores).

questions.model_answer:
a) Non-competitive inhibition of (1,3)-beta-D-glucan synthase, preventing synthesis of beta-1,3-D-glucan in the fungal cell wall, leading to osmotic lysis. Target absent in mammalian cells.
b) (1) Cryptococcus. (2) Fusarium. (3) Mucorales/zygomycetes. (Also: Trichosporon, dimorphic fungi, Pneumocystis cysts.)
c) (1) Urine/urinary tract. (2) Eye/vitreous.
d) Fungicidal against most Candida species (including many azole-resistant isolates), with higher MICs for C. parapsilosis and C. guilliermondii. Fungistatic against Aspergillus. No useful activity against Cryptococcus, Fusarium, Scedosporium, Trichosporon, zygomycetes, or dimorphic fungi. Active against Pneumocystis ascus (cyst) form but not trophic form (not used clinically).
e) (1) Candidemia and invasive candidiasis (first-line, including in non-neutropenic and neutropenic patients). (2) Esophageal candidiasis. (3) Empiric antifungal therapy in persistent febrile neutropenia. (4) Salvage/refractory invasive aspergillosis or when azoles/amphotericin are not tolerated.
f) Aspergillus spp. - Yes (fungistatic); Candida glabrata - Yes (usually susceptible, rising echinocandin resistance); Cryptococcus - No; Rhizopus - No; dimorphic fungi - No; Pneumocystis jirovecii - No (not clinically useful).

cohort_answer.text: a) Inhibit beta-glucan synthase enzyme responsible for (1,3)-beta-D-glucan synthesis which forms glucan polymers stabilizing cell wall. b) Cryptococcus spp.; Fusarium; Trichosporon spp.; Mucorales; PJP; dimorphics (limited activity). c) Eye; Urine. d) Yeasts: fungicidal vs Candida (exceptions elevated MICs in C. parapsilosis/guilliermondii, treatment failure reports with C. glabrata), not active vs cryptococcus. Dimorphic fungi: not active. Molds: fungistatic vs Aspergillus, not active vs Fusarium/paecilomyces/Trichosporon/Zygomycetes. e) Candidemia; aspergillosis (if refractory/intolerant to other therapies); empiric fungal coverage in prolonged febrile neutropenia. f) Aspergillus spp. - S (fungistatic); C. glabrata - usually S but increasing R; Cryptococcus - R; Rhizopus - R; Dimorphics - R; PCP - R.

questions.question: For amphotericin B and caspofungin, indicate Yes/No for reliable in vitro activity against each of the following organisms.
questions.question_raw: Q20 (2006 AM) Amphotericin B and Caspofungin. Write Y/N susceptibility in vitro for: Zygomycetes; Aspergillus fumigatus; Candida glabrata; Blastomyces dermatitidis; Cryptococcus neoformans

parts.text: Complete the susceptibility table (amphotericin B and caspofungin) for Zygomycetes, Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida glabrata, Blastomyces dermatitidis, and Cryptococcus neoformans.

questions.model_answer:
a) Susceptibility table (Y = reliable in vitro activity, N = not active):
(1) Zygomycetes (Mucorales): Amphotericin B = Yes; Caspofungin = No (echinocandins lack activity against Mucorales).
(2) Aspergillus fumigatus: Amphotericin B = Yes; Caspofungin = Yes (echinocandins are active against Aspergillus, though secondary to voriconazole/amphotericin for invasive disease).
(3) Candida glabrata: Amphotericin B = Yes; Caspofungin = Yes.
(4) Blastomyces dermatitidis: Amphotericin B = Yes; Caspofungin = No (echinocandins inactive against dimorphic endemic molds).
(5) Cryptococcus neoformans: Amphotericin B = Yes; Caspofungin = No (echinocandins lack activity; cryptococcal cell wall glucan synthesis not a useful target).

cohort_answer.text: Zygomycetes | Yes | No. Aspergillus fumigatus | Yes | Yes* (response rates 40-50%, not primary agent for invasive aspergillosis). Candida glabrata | Yes | Yes. Blastomyces dermatitidis | Yes | No. Cryptococcus neoformans | Yes | No.

questions.question: What is the molecular target of the following antifungals: posaconazole, micafungin, amphotericin, terbinafine?
questions.question_raw: PM 9. What is the molecular target of the following antifungals (4): Posaconazole, Micafungin, Amphotericin, Terbinafine

parts.text: State the molecular target of each antifungal.

parts_raw.text: State the molecular target of each antifungal

questions.model_answer: Posaconazole: lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (Erg11/CYP51), blocking lanosterol-to-ergosterol conversion. Micafungin: 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase (inhibits fungal cell wall glucan synthesis). Amphotericin: ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane — polyene binds ergosterol and forms pores, increasing permeability. Terbinafine: squalene epoxidase, an early enzyme in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway.

cohort_answer.text: Posaconazole - 14-alpha demethylase inhibitor (stops lanosterol to ergosterol). Micafungin - 1,3-beta-glucan synthetase enzyme inhibitor (fungal cell wall). Amphotericin - polyene, binds irreversibly to ergosterol in fungal cell membrane, increases permeability. Terbinafine - Squalene oxidase/epoxidase inhibitor (early step in ergosterol pathway).
